candidates.title: Compressing Sequences in the Latent Embedding Space: K-Token Merging for Large Language Models
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
candidates.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) incur significant computational and memory costs when processing long prompts, as full self-attention scales quadratically with input length. Token compression aims to address this challenge by reducing the number of tokens representing inputs. However, existing prompt-compression approaches primarily operate in token space and overlook inefficiencies in the latent embedding space. In this paper, we propose K-Token Merging, a latent-space compression framework that merges each contiguous block of K token embeddings into a single embedding via a lightweight encoder. The compressed sequence is processed by a LoRA-adapted LLM, while generation remains in the original vocabulary. Experiments on structural reasoning (Textualized Tree), sentiment classification (Amazon Reviews), and code editing (CommitPackFT) show that K-Token Merging lies on the Pareto frontier of performance vs. compression, achieving up to 75% input length reduction with minimal performance degradation. Code is available at https://github.com/shsjxzh/K-Token-Merging.

candidates.title: Invoke Interfaces Only When Needed: Adaptive Invocation for Large Language Models in Question Answering
candidates.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
candidates.abstract: The collaborative paradigm of large and small language models (LMs) effectively balances performance and cost, yet its pivotal challenge lies in precisely pinpointing the moment of invocation when hallucinations arise in small LMs. Previous optimization efforts primarily focused on post-processing techniques, which were separate from the reasoning process of LMs, resulting in high computational costs and limited effectiveness. In this paper, we propose a practical invocation evaluation metric called AttenHScore, which calculates the accumulation and propagation of hallucinations during the generation process of small LMs, continuously amplifying potential reasoning errors. By dynamically adjusting the detection threshold, we achieve more accurate real-time invocation of large LMs. Additionally, considering the limited reasoning capacity of small LMs, we leverage uncertainty-aware knowledge reorganization to assist them better capture critical information from different text chunks. Extensive experiments reveal that our AttenHScore outperforms most baselines in enhancing real-time hallucination detection capabilities across multiple QA datasets, especially when addressing complex queries. Moreover, our strategies eliminate the need for additional model training and display flexibility in adapting to various transformer-based LMs.

candidates.title: Multi-LLM Query Optimization
candidates.abstract: Deploying multiple large language models (LLMs) in parallel to classify an unknown ground-truth label is a common practice, yet the problem of optimally allocating queries across heterogeneous models remains poorly understood. In this paper, we formulate a robust, offline query-planning problem that minimizes total query cost subject to statewise error constraints which guarantee reliability for every possible ground-truth label. We first establish that this problem is NP-hard via a reduction from the minimum-weight set cover problem. To overcome this intractability, we develop a surrogate by combining a union bound decomposition of the multi-class error into pairwise comparisons with Chernoff-type concentration bounds. The resulting surrogate admits a closed-form, multiplicatively separable expression in the query counts and is guaranteed to be feasibility-preserving. We further show that the surrogate is asymptotically tight at the optimization level: the ratio of surrogate-optimal cost to true optimal cost converges to one as error tolerances shrink, with an explicit rate of $O\left(\log\log(1/\alpha_{\min}) / \log(1/\alpha_{\min})\right)$. Finally, we design an asymptotic fully polynomial-time approximation scheme (AFPTAS) that returns a surrogate-feasible query plan within a $(1+\varepsilon)$ factor of the surrogate optimum.

candidates.title: CatchUp: Depth-Aware Re-Admission of Visual Tokens for Efficient Large Vision-Language Models
candidates.abstract: Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) repeatedly process hundreds of visual tokens across decoder layers, incurring substantial computation and memory costs. Existing visual-token reduction methods often irreversibly discard tokens despite depth-varying query relevance. Although recoverable routing allows excluded tokens to return, re-admitted tokens retain stale hidden states after bypassing intermediate decoder transformations. Thus, token recoverability does not guarantee representation readiness at the current decoder depth. Under a fixed routing trajectory at a 64-token budget, replacing stale re-admitted states with current-depth oracle representations improves average RefCOCO Acc@0.5 from 18.96 to 23.18, revealing the impact of representation staleness. We propose CatchUp, a training-free framework combining reversible visual-token routing with Local Transition Correction (LTC). CatchUp repeatedly re-evaluates query-conditioned relevance over the complete visual-token set, preserving deferred tokens for later re-admission. LTC approximates their skipped representation evolution by transferring reference-to-current hidden-state transitions from semantically and spatially related active anchors. This correction improves alignment with current-depth oracle representations without recomputing the skipped decoder layers. Across three referring-expression grounding datasets and six multimodal benchmarks, CatchUp achieves the best grounding performance across all eight splits and the highest average multimodal retention among evaluated efficient methods at 64-, 128-, and 192-token budgets. At a 64-token budget, CatchUp processes 88.9% fewer active visual tokens per post-routing decoder interval, retains 92.17% of dense-model multimodal performance, and reduces end-to-end latency by 8.0%. Code is available at https://github.com/pej0918/CatchUp
candidates.reason: CatchUpは視覚トークンを不可逆に捨てず、深さごとにクエリ条件付き関連度を再評価して再入場させ、飛ばした層の表現進化を局所遷移補正で近似することで、64トークン予算でLVLMの計算・メモリを削減する学習不要の枠組みであり、マルチモーダル推論のトークン削減に直接貢献する。

candidates.title: Deploying Open-Source Large Language Models: A performance Analysis
candidates.abstract: Since the release of ChatGPT in November 2022, large language models (LLMs) have seen considerable success, including in the open-source community, with many open-weight models available. However, the requirements to deploy such a service are often unknown and difficult to evaluate in advance. To facilitate this process, we conducted numerous tests at the Centre Inria de l'Universit\'e de Bordeaux. In this article, we propose a comparison of the performance of several models of different sizes (mainly Mistral and LLaMa) depending on the available GPUs, using vLLM, a Python library designed to optimize the inference of these models. Our results provide valuable information for private and public groups wishing to deploy LLMs, allowing them to evaluate the performance of different models based on their available hardware. This study thus contributes to facilitating the adoption and use of these large language models in various application domains.
candidates.reason: オープンソースLLMのデプロイについて、Mistral・LLaMA等の複数モデルとGPU構成の組合せをvLLMで実測比較し、ハードウェアに応じた推論性能の見通しを与える性能分析であり、LLM推論基盤の計測に直接貢献する。
